★★★ `.section NAME` AND THE RESERVE-WITH-FILL FAMILY, READ BACK AT RUNTIME — the AArch64 half. ✔MEASURED 2026-08-13 under qemu-aarch64 (`QEMU_LD_PREFIX=/usr/aarch64-linux-gnu`): exit 42, debug AND release.

★★★ THE SECOND DIALECT IS THE ENTIRE REASON THIS FILE IS SEPARATE FROM ITS SIBLING, AND THE CLAIM IS AN EQUALITY OF NUMBERS. `.section` / `.space` / `.zero` / `.skip` are declared in BOTH `.lang.json` documents and handled by ONE engine; the DIRECTIVE text here is byte-identical to `asm_x86_64_section_reserve_fill_readback`'s and only the INSTRUCTIONS are this CPU's. ✔MEASURED: the two files produce the SAME nine exit codes across the SAME nine sweep arms (42 / 11 / 11 / 13 / 11 / 13 / 42 / 14 / 12). A mechanism witnessed by one dialect is the weaker claim this project keeps having to walk back.

★★★ WHY IT EXISTS, AS A MEASUREMENT. ✔MEASURED before it was written: `grep -rn '^\s*\.\(section\|space\|zero\|skip\)' examples/asm/*/main.s` returned NOTHING — both verbs shipped proven only by unit tests over an in-memory `dataItems` vector. A unit test cannot see whether those bytes reach the IMAGE, at the right OFFSETS, with the right CONTENTS. This repo has the scar: a lowering computed `dataItems` and the driver dropped them on the floor; the mutant compiled clean, produced an artifact, and only an image-level witness caught it.

★★ EVERY BYTE RESERVED IS LOADED AGAIN BY THE PROGRAM THAT RESERVED IT, and the answer is a SUM of what was read (20 + 7 + 15 + 0 = 42), not a constant. Each quadword is ALSO compared against what it must be and lands on its own numbered arm (11/12/13/14) when it is not — so a wrong byte cannot collide with 42 by arithmetic accident, and the failing arm says WHICH quadword was wrong.

★★★ THE DISCRIMINATION IS MEASURED, ARM BY ARM, UNDER qemu. ✔MEASURED 2026-08-13 by rebuilding this same file with ONE directive operand changed (each mutant checked byte-wise against the base before it was compiled, so an arm that failed to land is reported VOID rather than counted):
  • `.space 1, 20` -> `.space 1, 21`   exit 11  (the fill BYTE)
  • `.space 1, 20` -> `.space 1`       exit 11  (the fill DROPPED — what the verb did before it was modelled)
  • `.skip 7`      -> `.skip 6`        exit 11  (the reserve's SIZE)
  • `.quad 7`      -> `.quad 9`        exit 12  (the emitData that follows the reserves)
  • `.zero 1, 15`  -> `.zero 1, 0`     exit 13  (`.zero` carries a fill too)
  • `.space 7`     -> `.space 7, 1`    exit 13  (a fill appearing where none was named)
  • `.section .bss` -> `.section .data` exit 14 (the SECTION the operand names)
  • `.section .rodata` -> `.rodata`     REFUSED, A0008, 'is a SECTION NAME in this dialect, not a directive'
  ⓘ AND ONE CONTROL THAT MUST **NOT** MOVE: `.space 8, 3` -> `.space 8, 0` in `.bss` stays exit 42, because a zero-fill section stores no file bytes and BOTH fills are correctly ignored. An arm that changed here would mean the fill was reaching the wire, which is the defect in the other direction.

★★ THE `.bss` FILL IS WHAT MAKES THE SECTION'S IDENTITY RUNTIME-OBSERVABLE, and it is the reason that line names a fill it does not want. `.space 8, 3` in a zero-fill section is warned-and-ignored (gas does exactly this: `Warning: ignoring fill value in section '.bss'`, exit 0). Route that section to a file-backed one by mistake and the SAME directive writes eight 0x03 bytes — which is the `.section .bss` -> `.section .data` arm above, exit 14. Without the fill, that mutant would still exit 42 and the section's identity would have no runtime witness at all.
  ⓘ THE WARNING IS TOLERATED BY DESIGN, NOT BY LUCK: ✔MEASURED in `tests/examples/examples_runner.cpp`, the compile-side gate is `EXPECT_EQ(rep.errorCount(), 0u)` — ERROR severity only.

★★ WHAT THIS FIXTURE DOES **NOT** SEPARATE, said plainly rather than left to be discovered: `.rodata` versus `.data` is NOT distinguishable from inside the process without attempting a write, so a mutant routing `.section .rodata` to the `.data` row still exits 42. That property is pinned where it can be seen — `tests/asm/test_asm_text_to_lir.cpp` asserts `.section .rodata` reaches `DataSectionKind::Rodata` and `.section .data` reaches `Data`. The corpus adds what the unit tier cannot: that the bytes survive the section assignment, the linker's layout and the loader's mapping.

★★ `adr` REACHES ALL THREE SECTIONS, WHICH IS NOT FREE ON THIS CPU AND IS THEREFORE PART OF WHAT THIS FILE WITNESSES. AArch64's `adr` has a ±1 MiB range, so a symbol in `.rodata`, `.data` or `.bss` is reachable from `.text` only if the linker's layout keeps them within it. ✔MEASURED: it does, for all three, in an image this size.

⚠ NO x86_64 LEG HERE, DELIBERATELY: this file is AArch64 assembly and names AArch64 registers, so it is not portable text. Its sibling covers the x86_64 CPU and, being a pe64+elf64 pair, the second OBJECT FORMAT as well.

⚠ AND ONE DIALECT DIFFERENCE WORTH RECORDING RATHER THAN DISCOVERING: the flags/type refusal reaches a DIFFERENT SITE on the two dialects, because `@` is a token in the AT&T document (`.type foo, @function`) and is NOT one here (this dialect writes `%function`). ✔MEASURED: `.section .rodata,@progbits` gives A0008 'carries 2 operands' on x86_64 and `P000E: got illegal character 0x40` here, while `.section .rodata,1` and `.section .rodata,%progbits` reach A0008 on BOTH. Both refuse; only the message differs. See `tests/asm/test_asm_shipped_dialects.cpp`, which pins both paths on the SHIPPED documents.

★ THE `release` ARM, SCOPED HONESTLY. At the `encode` tier no MIR module exists, so the optimizer, the register allocator and calling-convention materialization never run — this arm does NOT witness the optimizer and cannot. It pins the narrower fact that `--config=release` still produces a working binary from assembly, and it is ✔MEASURED at 42 under qemu rather than assumed.

HONEST BY CONSTRUCTION: the source of this example IS assembly, so it is assembled without ever forming the HIR/MIR an optimizer pass runs on. No pipeline can transform it and no edit to this example could ever make this arm differ — the arm still earns its place by pinning that naming a pipeline does not BREAK an assembly example. Deliberately NOT given "mustDifferFromBaseline" — an honest no-op, not a missed opt-in.
